findings.text: The literal command `pnpm test -- tests/unit/evaluateDiagnosis.test.ts` forwards a literal `--` to vitest, which then ignores the file filter and runs the whole unit/api suite (8 files, 439 tests, all passed at that time, exit 0). The focused run `pnpm exec vitest run tests/unit/evaluateDiagnosis.test.ts` ran only this unit's file (44 tests, exit 0).

SIG-04 -> `dep` is decided from the risks list passed to the plan (the displayed risks, capped at 5), so the plan stays consistent with what the result shows. With rules v1 SIG-04 (score 12) can never be dropped by the cap: at most six signals can fire together and the dropped one is SIG-07 (score 8).

messages.text: evaluateDiagnosis(input: DiagnosisInput, rules: Rules): DiagnosisResult is exported from shared/domain/evaluateDiagnosis.ts. It is pure, takes no clock, db or network, and returns plain JSON-safe data with rulesVersion = rules.version (rulesV1.version is 1). The persistence/service layer should call it with rulesV1 at completion and store the whole result plus rulesVersion; a past result must never be recomputed with newer rules (RULE-dm-11).

DiagnosisResult.plan holds ActionKey values only. Resolve the texts with ACTION_CATALOG[key] (title, reason, howTo) from shared/content/actionCatalog.ts; the risks resolve with getRiskInfo(signalId) and the stage/lock texts with shared/content/stageContent.ts. shared/domain/actionPlan.ts also exports buildActionPlan and isInvestEligible if a caller needs the plan rules on their own.

tests/fixtures/rulesV2.ts exports rulesV2: rulesV1 with version 2 and stage3.minProductChannel 70. A case with Produto e canal at 67 (G3 with pc1, pc2, pc3 all 2) is stage 3 / lock co / plan [co, invest, pc] under v1 and stage 2 / lock pc / plan [pc, co, mm] under v2, so it can drive the persistence test for AC-dm-22 and the comparison test for AC-dm-31.

Not run by this unit (belongs to integration): tests/api/diagnosisRoutes.test.ts (the capability verification command lists it; it is owned by another unit), AC-dm-22 persistence with a rules swap, AC-dm-19/21/23/24/49 e2e checks and the AC-dm-27 timing measurement in the Play on Windows.
